text:
maria: heads-up — seeing a burst of GPU alloc latency in eu-west dedicated pool around 12:10UTC, multiple tenants queued, tail latency ~3x. anyone else?
ryan: I see the spike in allocator histograms. linking grafana panel: https://grafana.internal/r/allocs?orgId=1&from=now-30m&to=now
asha: noticed increased NIC qlen and RX drops on nodes eu-west-a3..a6 around same time. suspect cross-az spillover when az-balance evicted jobs.
leo: can you paste the node logs? curious if kubelet preemption or our soft-evict loop triggered.
maria: paste of kube events around 12:09: 
```
kubectl get events -n infra --field-selector involvedObject.name=node-eu-west-a3 --since=20m
12:09 Preempted Pod/tenant-123 on node-eu-west-a3 reason: EvictionThreshold
12:09 CNI: heavy retransmits on eth0
```
ryan: promql check I ran: `sum(rate(gpu_alloc_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (pool)` shows dedicated-eu-west jumped. also `sum(increase(node_network_receive_errors_total[5m])) by (instance)` correlates.
dmitri: this smells like "spill-to-az" routing doing the right thing but saturating NICs on the target AZ. when local capacity is low we route to sibling az until warmup completes.
asha: exactly — we warm up slices by transferring KV cache across nodes which pumps inter-az egress and increases cold KV misses, amplifying GPU busy time.
leo: quick mitigation options: 1) reduce cross-az spillover threshold to 0.5 so less cross-az routing, 2) enable soft-affinity backpressure to queue locally, 3) bump dedicated pool capacity for the impacted tenant(s).
maria: cost/ops tradeoff: bumping capacity buys latency but costs $$$. prefer short-term routing throttle + tune warmup to be less chatty.
ryan: can we change soft-affinity config live? the flag is `routing.spillover.enabled` and `routing.spillover.threshold` in configmap `infra-routing`.
asha: I can push a conservative change: `threshold=0.35`, `max_concurrent_spillover=2` to limit concurrency. will roll canary to 10% of routing agents first.
dmitri: also propose we add a KV warmup backoff: exponential retry with jitter so we don't thrash inter-az links.
leo: good. can we also add a short-lived egress QoS for spillover traffic to protect system control plane? set DSCP for kv-sync to 34?
maria: ops-bot — create incident channel and page oncall with notes.
ops-bot: Created #incident-eu-west-spillover-1712349999 and paged oncall (ryan). Summary: alloc latency spike, suspected cross-az spillover + NIC saturation, mitigation plan = routing throttle canary + kv warmup backoff.
ryan: rolling the routing canary now to 10%... `kubectl apply -f infra-routing-canary.yaml`
asha: canary applied. monitoring alert set: `alert if alloc_latency_p95 > 200ms for 3m` and `alert if node_rx_err_rate > baseline*5 for 2m`.
maria: early signal: p95 dropped ~35% after canary, NIC errors trending down.
dmitri: nice. follow-ups: 1) permanent tune for spillover thresholds and warmup backoff, 2) run a synthetic KV warming job across AZs to validate egress load, 3) run cost calc for short-term capacity vs risk.
leo: I'll own the synthetic test, estimate egress megabytes and QPS.
asha: I'll open a PR with config changes and run a 30% canary then full roll once synthetic passes.
ryan: if things calm in 30m we revert any capacity bumps. otherwise we'll escalate to sales for impacted tenants.
maria: thanks all. tagging follow-ups in the incident channel. :thumbsup:
